tech.description: An academic hall with 6 program slots. Six programs of one school in one hall found that school.

tech.name: MED 501 · Foundations of Human Medicine
tech.description: Opens medical training with the body as a system, from cell to organ, and with the history, examination, and patient interview every later year builds on. Founds the medical school (MD); offered once every Health Science course is taught and the Medical Center stands, and taught there.

tech.name: MED 510 · Gross Anatomy & Histology
tech.description: Works through dissection alongside the microscope, so students learn each structure both where it lies and what its tissue is made of.

tech.name: MED 520 · Pathophysiology & Pharmacotherapy
tech.description: Pairs each disease's mechanism with the drugs that interrupt it, so dosing, interactions, and side effects are learned with the illness they treat.

tech.name: MED 530 · Clinical Neurology
tech.description: Localizes lesions from the bedside examination, then confirms them with imaging, across stroke, seizure, dementia, and disorders of movement.

tech.name: MED 540 · Evidence-Based Practice & Population Medicine
tech.description: Teaches students to read a trial critically, weigh screening and prevention across a population, and decide when the evidence should change practice.

tech.name: MED 550 · Clerkship & Residency Preparation
tech.description: Readies students for the wards with note-writing, case presentations, and handoffs, and for internship with the residency application and the Match.

tech.name: MED 560 · Immunology & Infectious Disease
tech.description: Covers how the immune system recognizes and remembers a threat, how pathogens evade it, and how vaccines and antimicrobials tip the balance.

tech.name: MED 570 · Medical Genetics & Genomics
tech.description: Reads inheritance and the genome clinically, through family pedigrees, carrier screening, and exome sequencing, and the counseling each result requires.

tech.name: MED 580 · Psychiatry & Behavioral Medicine
tech.description: Diagnoses and treats mental illness alongside the behaviors, from sleep to substance use, that shape every other illness a patient has.

tech.name: MED 590 · Surgical Principles & Perioperative Care
tech.description: Prepares students for the operating room, from consent and sterile technique to anesthesia, wound healing, and the complications of the days after.

tech.name: MED 600 · Global & Public Health Systems
tech.description: Compares how countries pay for, staff, and ration health care, and why outcomes differ so widely between systems that spend alike.

tech.name: MED 610 · Advanced Clinical Practicum
tech.description: Rotates students through internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, and family medicine, then gives them patients of their own as sub-interns.

tech.name: LAW 501 · Foundations of American Law
tech.description: Introduces the sources of American law, how courts reason from precedent, and the legal writing and case briefing every later class assumes. Founds the law school (JD); offered once every Social Sciences & Humanities course is taught and the Law School stands, and taught there.

tech.name: LAW 510 · Contracts & Torts
tech.description: Covers when a promise binds and what breaking it costs, and when an act, whether intentional, careless, or merely dangerous, becomes a wrong.

tech.name: LAW 520 · Civil Procedure & Evidence
tech.description: Follows a lawsuit from the complaint through discovery and trial, and the rules that decide which facts a jury is ever allowed to hear.

tech.name: LAW 530 · Constitutional Law Seminar
tech.description: Turns the Commerce Clause, due process, and equal protection into tests a brief applies, and argues the cases as counsel did before the Court.

tech.name: LAW 540 · Legal Clinic & Advocacy
tech.description: Puts students in front of real clients under supervision, drafting, negotiating, and appearing in court on cases the college takes on.

tech.name: LAW 550 · Property & Real Estate Law
tech.description: Covers ownership, leases, easements, and land use, and the title searches, mortgages, and closings that move real estate between hands.

tech.name: LAW 560 · Criminal Law & Procedure
tech.description: Examines what makes conduct a crime and the constitutional limits on search, interrogation, and trial that bind the state in proving it.

tech.name: LAW 570 · Comparative & International Law
tech.description: Compares the common law with civil-law codes, then turns to the treaties, custom, and courts that govern relations among states.

tech.name: MBA 501 · Managerial Foundations
tech.description: Grounds the MBA in accounting, economics, and organizational behavior, so students from any background share one working vocabulary. Founds the MBA program; offered once every Business course is taught and the Business School stands, and taught there.

tech.name: MBA 510 · Corporate Finance & Valuation
tech.description: Values companies and projects the way investors do, and decides how a firm should raise money, spend it, and return it to shareholders.

tech.name: MBA 520 · Marketing Strategy
tech.description: Chooses which customers to serve and how to win them against rivals, from segmentation and positioning to pricing and brand.

tech.name: MBA 530 · Operations & Business Analytics
tech.description: Models supply chains, queues, and capacity, and uses data to decide where a business should cut waste and where it should add slack.

tech.name: MBA 540 · Capstone Consulting Practicum
tech.description: Sends student teams to advise a real organization on a live problem, ending in recommendations presented to its leadership.

tech.name: PHDE 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in Engineering
tech.description: Prepares doctoral students to frame a research question, design experiments and simulations to answer it, and defend the result to peers. Founds the engineering doctorate (PhD); offered once every Engineering course is taught and the Graduate College stands, and taught there.

tech.name: PHDE 710 · Advanced Continuum & Structural Theory
tech.description: Derives the mechanics of solids and fluids from first principles, and applies them to structures and materials at the limits of design.

tech.name: PHDE 720 · Doctoral Seminar in Applied Electromagnetics
tech.description: Treats wave propagation, antennas, and electromagnetic compatibility at research depth, with papers from the field presented each week.

tech.name: PHDE 730 · Dissertation Research in Engineering
tech.description: Registers the candidate each term until the experiments are done, the chapters are written, and the committee signs off.

tech.name: PHDS 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in the Sciences
tech.description: Covers experimental design, statistics, and the ethics of research that every doctoral scientist needs before starting a laboratory project. Founds the natural-sciences doctorate (PhD); offered once every Science course is taught and the Graduate College stands, and taught there.

tech.name: PHDS 710 · Advanced Quantum & Statistical Theory
tech.description: Builds quantum mechanics and statistical physics to the level where current research papers in either field can be read and extended.

tech.name: PHDS 720 · Advanced Synthesis & Structure Determination
tech.description: Plans multistep syntheses and proves what was made, with spectroscopy and crystallography read directly from the instruments.

tech.name: PHDS 730 · Dissertation Research in the Natural Sciences
tech.description: Ends in a public defense and the graduate school's acceptance of the final copy, after however many years the research takes.

tech.name: PHDH 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in Health Science
tech.description: Trains doctoral students in study design, biostatistics, and research ethics for work that involves patients and populations. Founds the health-science doctorate (PhD); offered once every Health Science course is taught and the Graduate College stands, and taught there.

tech.name: PHDH 710 · Systems & Cognitive Neuroscience Seminar
tech.description: Presents and critiques current papers on the circuits behind cognition, weighing what imaging, optogenetics, and population recording can each show about cause.

tech.name: PHDH 720 · Translational Clinical Research
tech.description: Carries a finding from the laboratory into a clinical trial, with the regulatory, statistical, and ethical steps between the two.

tech.name: PHDH 730 · Dissertation Research in Health Science
tech.description: Takes a question of the student's own through a proposal, data collection, and three publishable papers to the final defense.

tech.name: PHDC 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in Computing
tech.description: Prepares doctoral students to read the literature, run reproducible experiments, and write papers that computing conferences will accept. Founds the computing doctorate (PhD); offered once every Computer Science course is taught and the Graduate College stands, and taught there.

tech.name: PHDC 710 · Advanced Seminar in Learning Theory
tech.description: Studies what can be learned from data and how fast, with the generalization bounds and optimization results behind modern machine learning.

tech.name: PHDC 720 · Foundations of Computation
tech.description: Covers computability, complexity classes, and the limits they set on what any algorithm, however clever, can ever achieve.

tech.name: PHDC 730 · Dissertation Research in Computing
tech.description: Turns a series of peer-reviewed conference papers into a dissertation, with the experiments rerun until a committee is satisfied.

tech.name: PHDL 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in the Humanities
tech.description: Trains doctoral students in archives, close reading, and the conventions of scholarly argument across the humanities. Founds the humanities doctorate (PhD); offered once every Social Sciences & Humanities course is taught and the Graduate College stands, and taught there.

tech.name: PHDL 710 · Advanced Seminar in Literary Theory
tech.description: Reads Derrida, Foucault, and Spivak whole rather than in excerpt, and the affective and ecological turns that have since argued with them.

tech.name: PHDL 720 · Doctoral Seminar in Social Theory
tech.description: Works through the classic and current theories of how societies hold together, change, and divide, from Durkheim to the present.

tech.name: PHDL 730 · Dissertation Research in the Humanities
tech.description: Supports the dissertation itself: a book-length work of original humanities scholarship, defended before a committee.

tech.name: PhD 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in Economics
tech.description: Covers the econometrics, identification strategies, and data work that doctoral research in economics is judged on. Founds the economics doctorate (PhD); offered once every Business course is taught and the Graduate College stands, and taught there.

tech.name: PhD 710 · Advanced Microeconomic Theory
tech.description: Builds consumer, producer, and general-equilibrium theory with the mathematics used in current research, from game theory to mechanism design.

tech.name: PhD 720 · Doctoral Seminar in Financial Economics
tech.description: Reads current research on asset pricing, corporate finance, and financial crises, and presents it to the seminar each week.

tech.name: PhD 730 · Dissertation Research in Economics
tech.description: Assembles three original papers into a dissertation, and sends the strongest out as the job-market paper a candidate presents at every interview.

tech.name: MFA 701 · Graduate Studio Practice
tech.description: Gives each artist a studio of their own and a weekly critique, where the work is made, shown, and argued over by peers and faculty. Founds the MFA program; offered once every Arts & Media course is taught and the Arts Center stands, and taught there.

tech.name: MFA 710 · Advanced Fiction & Poetry Workshop
tech.description: Critiques a new manuscript from each writer every few weeks, alongside craft reading chosen for what that writer's work is attempting.

tech.name: MFA 720 · Graduate Composition Seminar
tech.description: Brings new scores before performers and peers each week, from the first sketch to a finished work ready for the concert hall.

tech.name: MFA 730 · Thesis Exhibition & Production
tech.description: Culminates the degree in a public exhibition, performance, or publication, mounted by the student and reviewed by the faculty.

tech.name: Meadow House
tech.description: The college's first residence hall — build it to give students somewhere to live on campus.

tech.name: Lakeside House
tech.description: A house of entryways rather than corridors, with an RA on the first floor of each. Freshmen ask for these by name. Adds 500 beds.

tech.name: Riverside House
tech.description: A residence hall: four stories of ranked windows and balconies under one long roof. Adds 500 beds.

tech.name: Hillcrest House
tech.description: Suites behind a real front door: quieter than the halls, with a kitchenette to each floor and a lounge nobody books. Adds 500 beds.

tech.name: Cascade House
tech.description: An apartment building, flat-roofed and balconied: kitchens and a lock on every door, the kind of housing upperclassmen ask for. Adds 500 beds.

tech.name: Summit House
tech.description: A residential college: a thousand beds around one formal front door, built in the stone the college keeps for its best. The old answer to everything, at the old price. Adds 1,000 beds.

tech.name: Vanguard House
tech.description: A six-story apartment building with a balcony to every other apartment. Adds 1,000 beds.

tech.name: Sterling House
tech.description: A high-rise residence hall: twice the beds on more ground, six stories of ranked windows and balconies. Adds 1,000 beds.

tech.name: Crestline House
tech.description: Six stories of suites behind a formal door: the residence seniors ask for. Adds 1,000 beds.

tech.name: Overlook Village
tech.description: A residential village: a dozen small houses around a shared green, on one large plot. Adds 1,500 beds.

tech.name: Ridgeline Village
tech.description: A residential village in brick: a dozen houses and a common house around a shared green, on one large plot. Adds 1,500 beds.

tech.name: Meridian Tower
tech.description: A residential tower with shops and a food hall at street level. Adds 5,000 beds, and feeds 1,500 students from its shops.

tech.name: Beacon Tower
tech.description: A residential tower lit at the top, with shops and a food hall at street level. Adds 5,000 beds, and feeds 1,500 students from its shops.

tech.name: Horizon Tower
tech.description: A residential tower with a roof terrace, and shops and a food hall at street level. Adds 5,000 beds, and feeds 1,500 students from its shops.

tech.name: Aurora Tower
tech.description: The tallest residential tower on campus, under a glass crown, with shops and a food hall at street level. Adds 5,000 beds, and feeds 1,500 students from its shops.

tech.name: The Original Commons
tech.description: The college's first dining hall — build it to feed the founding class. Serves 350 students.

tech.name: Union Square Eatery
tech.description: Serves 900 more students.

tech.name: Commons Cafeteria
tech.description: Serves 1,800 more students.

tech.name: The Grand Table
tech.description: Serves 3,000 more students.

tech.name: Old Well Commons
tech.description: Serves 5,000 more students.

tech.name: Waterside Commons
tech.description: Serves 8,000 more students.

tech.name: Harborview Market
tech.description: Serves 12,000 more students.

tech.name: Central Dining Pavilion
tech.description: Serves 16,000 more students.

tech.name: Campus Grocery Store
tech.description: A full grocery store for 17,500 students — a second basic-needs option alongside the dining halls, though with the towers' shops it covers 40% of meals at most. Can be built once enrollment passes 8,000.

tech.name: Library
tech.description: Study seats and stacks for 1,200 students.

tech.name: Student Center
tech.description: Social space for 1,000 students — happier students mean a bigger applicant pool next cycle.

tech.name: Student Union Expansion
tech.description: Adds 3,000 more social capacity.

tech.name: Recreation Center
tech.description: Recreation and intramural space for 1,200 students: social life, and a little prestige.

tech.name: Gym & Fitness Center
tech.description: Weight room and cardio floor for 4,000 students.

tech.name: Swimming Pool
tech.description: An outdoor Olympic-length pool and its deck, for 3,000 students.

tech.name: Tennis Courts
tech.description: Courts open to 2,000 students.

tech.name: Athletics Complex
tech.description: The last of the fitness buildings: a complex keeping 3,500 more students fit, and a bigger prestige lift, though not a competition venue. Can be built at prestige 55.

tech.name: Art Gallery
tech.description: A rotating-exhibit gallery for 500 students, and the venue Studio Art's capstone courses exhibit in.

tech.name: Multi-Sport Field
tech.description: A competition-grade outdoor field for 700 students' worth of social capacity, shared by soccer, lacrosse, field hockey, and track and field.

tech.name: Arena
tech.description: An indoor competition arena for 1,400 students' worth of social capacity, shared by basketball, volleyball and ice hockey.

tech.name: Baseball & Softball Diamond
tech.description: A regulation diamond for 500 students' worth of social capacity, shared by baseball and softball.

tech.name: Natatorium
tech.description: A competition pool for 550 students' worth of social capacity — distinct from the rec Swimming Pool, and where swim & dive and water polo compete.

tech.name: Football Stadium
tech.description: The pinnacle varsity venue: a full football stadium, and 2,500 students' worth of social capacity. Listed once football goes varsity.

tech.name: Field House
tech.description: Weight rooms, an indoor training floor and treatment rooms for every varsity program at once — 800 students' worth of social capacity, and a lift to every team the college fields.

tech.name: Health & Counseling Center
tech.description: Care for 2,000 students. Can be built once enrollment passes 1,500.

tech.name: University Clinic
tech.description: Full outpatient care for 6,000 more students, and the practicum site Nursing's and Pharmacy's clinical coursework trains in. Can be built once enrollment passes 6,000.

tech.name: Medical Center
tech.description: A teaching hospital with the college's name over the door, caring for 30,000 more students: where the MD's clerkship year is spent, and a lift to the college's academics and research while it stands. Opens from Year 15, for a campus past 20,000 students enrolled.

tech.name: Campus Quad
tech.description: A green centerpiece for campus life. Cheap, and worth it at any size — its contribution never dilutes as enrollment grows.

tech.name: Grand Quad & Gardens
tech.description: A landscaped centerpiece expansion: more social life, at any size.

tech.name: The Founder's Statue
tech.description: The founder in bronze on a stone plinth, a little larger than life, and a meeting place from the day it goes up.

tech.name: The Fountain
tech.description: A basin and a jet on a paved circle: somewhere to sit, and the first photograph on every tour.

tech.name: The Japanese Garden
tech.description: A koi pond under a red bridge, a torii over the path, a three-tiered pagoda, a stone lantern and cherry trees in blossom: the quietest acre on campus.

tech.name: The Chapel
tech.description: A small stone chapel, used for concerts and quiet as often as for services.

tech.name: The Bell Tower
tech.description: A slim tower with a peal of bells that marks the hours across the campus.

tech.name: The Arts Center
tech.description: A concert hall, two theaters and the studios behind them, under one roof and open late: the building the town comes to the college for, and the home of the MFA. Opens from Year 10, once every Arts & Media course is taught.

tech.name: The Research Park
tech.description: Laboratories at the edge of campus where faculty and industry work side by side. Once it stands, any lab can take on a Landmark Program. At a college specialized in research, its Landmark work fills research's specialization share and every lab's output is 15% higher; a park at a college specialized in anything else keeps its Landmark Programs and adds nothing more. Opens once the college is specialized in research and every lab on campus has finished a research project; no other college may build it.

tech.name: The Graduate College
tech.description: A quadrangle of its own for graduate students, with a hall to dine in and a tower to be seen from: the home of the six doctorates. Opens from Year 15, once any school's undergraduate courses are all taught.

tech.name: The Law School
tech.description: A courthouse of a building, with a moot court, a law library and a portico to argue under: the home of the School of Law. Opens from Year 15, once every Social Sciences & Humanities course is taught.

tech.name: The Business School
tech.description: Glass, a trading floor and an atrium where recruiters wait: the home of the MBA. Opens from Year 15, once every Business course is taught.

tech.name: The Faculty Training Institute
tech.description: Seminar rooms, a teaching studio with cameras at the back and a faculty lounge where old hands talk shop with new ones. Each year it takes professors for a term, and they come back a full grade better in the classroom. Opens once the college is specialized in academics; no other college may build it.

tech.name: The Athletic Performance Complex
tech.description: A glass-walled training center beside the venues: a strength hall, a sports-science lab, recovery pools, film rooms and a running track on the roof, where every varsity athlete trains. At a college specialized in athletics it carries 2 more flagship programs than the subsidy level allows, its scholarships recruit 17% more, its teams play stronger in a semifinal and a final, and its deep runs fill athletics' specialization share. Opens once the college is specialized in athletics; no other college may build it.

tech.name: The University Museum
tech.description: Decades of gifts, loans and bequests finally in one place and on show: a museum that schoolchildren are taken to and graduates bring their own children back to. Opens from Year 40, or Year 35 for a college at prestige 100.

tech.name: The Campanile
tech.description: A bell tower taller than anything for miles: the college on every postcard, and a clock the town sets its watches by.

tech.name: The Great Dome
tech.description: A domed rotunda over a great hall, the kind of room people travel to stand in.

tech.name: The Triumphal Gate
tech.description: An arch at the head of the campus with the college's name cut across it: the way every graduate walks out.

tech.name: Zeta Phi Psi House
tech.description: The dedicated chapter house built for Zeta Phi Psi.
